#dayshiro 26.08.08  오늘의 마시로씨는 무려 아침부터 왔어요! 일정으로 바쁘다더니 어찌 이런 이른 시간부터 오셨는지 감사함을 담아 바로 착석!  분명 쿨러 문제로 컴퓨터에 문제가 있다 했는데? 그런 것 치곤  멀쩡해보이는 아침 뱅송 뭐, 저챗 정도는 괜찮나 싶어 대화를 이어 나가 보지만... 결국 캠조차 켜지 않았음에도 엄청나게 버벅이기 시작하더니, cpu 온도가 100도를 넘어갔다 한다 이러다 큰 일이 날 듯싶어 부랴부랴 아침 방송은 여기서 종료 다행히 이번에는 스페가 가능할 거 같다는 말에 얌전히 오늘 저녁을 기다려 보는데...  6시가 지나고, 7시가 지나고... 음, 왜 마시로 씨에게서 알림이 오지 않을까? 전전긍긍하던 그때! 알림은 전혀 예상치 못한 곳에서 왔으니! 네? 치지직에서요? 왜요? 헐레벌떡 달려가 보니 한껏 밝아진 모습의 마시로 씨가 우리를 반긴다 무사히 쿨러를 교체해 드디어 온도 문제를 해결했다는 마시로 씨 그러면서 로켓배송을 해 준 쿠팡 찬양을 잠깐 해 준다 그러고 나서 오늘은 짧방을 하기로 했으니 테스트 겸 오버워치를 해보기로 하는 마시로 씨 전날 싹 다 포맷을 한 탓에 아무것도 남아 있지 않아, 오버워치를 설치하며 방송 설정을 다시 잡아보기로 한다 그러면서 화면 전환 애니메이션을 예전에 사용하던 우주선으로 바꿔본다 다시보기로밖에 접해본 적이 없는 뉴비 마로로서는 나름 신선한 애니메이션이었다 무척 귀엽기도 했고 아쉽게도 나팔 소리 등 포맷으로 인해 몇 가지 도구를 잃어버렸다는 마시로 씨 다시 또 처음부터 쌓아가야겠다며 한탄을 한다 그러고는 쿨러 설치 중 있었던 해프닝을 짧게 이야기해준다 쿨러 설치를 살짝 잘못한 까닭에 cpu 온도가 100도를 넘어가자 설마 cpu를 바꿔야 하나, 잠시 등골이 오싹해졌다 한다 요즘 같이 컴퓨터 부품이 비싸진 때에 정말 소름이 돋는 이야기가 아닐 수 없다 쿨러를 다시 설치하고 나서야 다행히 정상적으로 온도가 떨어졌다고 한다 부품 문제인지 모르고 괜히 포맷을 했다며 후회하지만, 덕분에 컴퓨터가 조금은 가벼워졌으니 다행이라며 나름 위안을 삼아본다 (그래, 그래 머릿결도 전보다 더 찰랑거리고 피부도 더 탱글해졌네) 아무래도 이런 일이 발생했으니 설정을 도와주시는 분께 투컴에 물어본 듯한 마시로 씨  디코로 정보 유출 위험이 있는 것이 아닌 이상, 현재 컴퓨터 스펙에 컴퓨터를 하나 더 추가할 필요 없다는 답변을 받았다 한다 이걸로 돈을 아끼게 됐으니 나름 이득인가? 워낙 아침부터 쿨러 문제로 긴장한 탓에 제대로 식사를 하지 못했을 거란 우리의 예상과 달리, 아침으로 까르보 불닭을 먹은 후 야무지게 순대국밥까지 한 그릇 때렸다 한다 (잘 먹었으니 다행이긴 한데... 왜 꼭 긴장해서 굶은 것같이 말한 거야?) 그러는 사이 오버워치 다운로드가 끝나고 새로운 마음으로 게임 스타트! 맥... 캐서디 실력을 뽐내며 본인의 실력을 맘껏 뽐내는 마시로 씨 그러나 어딘가 나사 빠진 것 같은 팀원들의 실력과 4~5분 넘게 걸리는 대기 시간에 별 수 없이 탱커로 전환한다  나름 자리야로 좋은 모습을 보였지만, 팀원이 단체로 탈주를 하거나 이길 수 있는 게임을 지는 등 답답한 상황이 연달아 터진다 결국, 본인은 캐서디 원챔을 하겠다며 제자리로 돌아간 마시로 씨 하지만, 여전히 긴 대기 시간에 오버워치는 여기까지만 하기로 한다  비록 짧방이라고는 하나 아직은 가기 이르다 생각했는지 짧게 저챗을 하자는 마시로 씨 일요일은 휴방이니 넘어가고, 다음 주 월요일에 무엇을 할까 잠시 이야기를 나눠 보는데... 이전 이야기가 나왔던 공포 게임, Corpse Party를 할까 생각 중이라 한다 그런데 이 게임... 플레이 타임이 10시간 정도라, 부지런히 깬다면 하루 안에 깰 수 있다 마시로 씨는 판단한다 그래서 잠시 짧은 투표라는 이름의 통파 타임이 시작되었고, 투표 결과 하루 안에 끝내는 것으로 의견이 좁혀졌다 (다행히 이번에는 무사히 돌아온 통파) 그렇게 월요일 방송은 조금 이른 시간에 시작되는가 싶었으나... 본인의 치과 예약을 까먹은 상태로 진행된 이야기였기에 투표는 아예 무효가 돼 버렸다 이런 촌극 끝에 월요일 방송은 4시에 시작하는 것으로 일단락 뭐, 정기 시간보다 빠르게 하는 거니 결국 투표대로 된 건가? 그러면서 화요일 일정까지 정하는 마시로 씨 peak의 마지막 업데이트가 화요일에 출시될 예정이라는 소식에 그날은 peak를 하기로 한다 근데... 아무리 생각해도 발표한 시간대가 미국을 기준으로 한 것이 아닐까 싶은데... 그렇다 해도 뭐, 겨우 하루 정도 미루어지는 정도니 크게 문제 되진 않을까 싶다 만약 밀린다해도 아직 보따리 안에는 3개의 게임이 준비되어 있다고 하니  잠시 앞으로의 일정을 간단히 정리하고, 게임을 하나 더 해 보기로 한다 그래서 꺼낸 게임은 Supermarket Chaos 일전에 타비님께서 추천해 주신 게임으로, 이 또한 언제가 할 게임 후보에 들어갔던 것이었다 아무래도 오늘이 그날이라 판단했는지 시작된 오늘의 두 번째 게임 게임 자체는 흩어진 물건들을 모아 정해진 선반에 돌려놓는 간단하지만, 엄청난 노가다가 예상되는 게임이었다 4000개가 넘는 물건을 언제 하나하나 정리하나 막막했으나, 제법 유용한 스킬이 있어 걱정했던 것보다 수월히 게임을 진행할 수 있었다 이런저런 노가리를 까며 자신이 직접 선곡한 플레이리스트를 자랑하기 시작한다 그러면서 자신의 선곡 센스가 얼마나 뛰어난지 자화자찬하는 마시로 씨 (그러니까 제발 공유 좀...) 잔잔한 음악을 배경으로 하며 묵묵히 선반을 채워 나갔지만, 점점 시간이 늦어지게 되자 이상 행동을 보이기 시작한다 이상한 텐션으로 노래를 흥얼거리거나, 뜬금없는 소리를 하는 등 명백히 피곤해 보이는 모습을 보이는 마시로 씨 (중간 중간 마로를 억까하는 건 늘 있던 일이니까 그러려니 하고) 그럼에도 선반을 가득 채우기 위해 애를 썼고, 점점 선반이 채워지게 되면서 오히려 마로들이 채우지 말라며 들고 일어섰다 그런 우리의 노력에도 결국 선반 채우기를 끝낸 마시로 씨 이 모든 일의 원흉인 로봇이 등장하며 또 한 번 사고를 일으키나 싶었지만, 별 어려움 없이 이를 제압하며 게임 클리어!  오랜 방송 시간으로 이제는 방송을 꺼보려는 마시로 씨 그러나 여전히 굶주려 있는 마로들은 쉬이 보낼 생각이 없는 모양이다 적어도 노래방을 해 달라는 요청에 잠시 고민하다 그러기로 하는 마시로 씨 그러면서 부르는 노래가 동요라니... 분명 자장가로써 훌륭한 선택이 아닐 수 없었다 단지, 그것을 부르는 사람이 마시로 씨였고, 너무나 귀여운 목소리로 노래하는 바람에 마로들을 더욱 자극했을 뿐... 그 탓에 3곡이나 더 부르게 된 마시로 씨... 아기 공룡 둘리 노래를 깜찍하게 마무리하며 오늘의 방송을 종료해 본다 그러자 쏟아지는 도네에 잠시 딜레이가 있었으나 무사히 오늘의 방송도 마무리가 되었다  분명 녹음 일정에 많이 지쳐 있었을 텐데, 늦은 시간까지 방송해 줘서 고마워! 다행히 오늘은 쉬는 날이니 늦게까지 푹 자도록 하자! 나도 아마 이걸 쓰고 나면 평소보다 늦은 시간에 일어날 것 같아... 정말 어제 아침부터 오늘 새벽까지 고생 많았어! 오늘은 침대에서 뒹굴며 조금은 게으르게 보내 보자!  그리고 내 그림에 리트윗과 답글을 남겨줘서 정말 고마워! 부족한 실력이라 시로의 눈에 띄지 않을 거라 생각했는데, 보기 좋게 내 예상을 깼네 덕분에 조금 더 자신감이 생긴 것 같아 오늘 하루 종일 너무 설레였던 탓에 정신이 나간 상태였다니까? 그 탓에 도네 타이밍이 꼬인 것 같아 그건 조금 아쉽구만요 시로 방송에서 채팅을 많이 쳐야지 하면서도 혹 상처가 되거나 방송에 방해가 되지 않을까 조심하다 보니 전보다 채팅량이 줄었네 거기에 좀 더 센스 있는 채팅을 치고 싶다는 욕심도 있다보니 번번히 타이밍을 놓치기도 하고 말이야 아무래도 더 오래 시로를 보고 싶다는 마음에 채팅 하나에도 생각을 많이 하게 됐나 봐 다음 방송부터는 좀 더 편안한 마음으로 참여할 수 있도록 할게! 그렇다고 막 나가겠다는 말은 아니고...  졸음에 머리가 멍한 탓인지 그냥 주저리 주러리 떠들고 있네...  수고 많았고! 푹 자고 일어나면 맛있는 밥 먹고 잘 쉬자!

WordPress supply chain attack hits 7 BdThemes plugins via poisoned API response, delivering webshells and rogue admin accounts to every site running the Biggopti banner component, active since June 23, 2026.  - No plugin files were modified on disk. Attackers gained write access to BdThemes' DigitalOcean Spaces bucket and replaced legitimate JSON served from api.sigmative[.]io with crafted payloads exploiting an unescaped display_id field (CVSS 5.4, unpatched) in the Biggopti admin banner component. The XSS fires in every admin browser on every wp-admin page load, making file-integrity scanners blind to the compromise.  - The attack chain is multi-stage: XSS triggers a fetch to ia-cdn[.]com/fz/w2.js, which creates a rogue admin via the WP REST API, installs a webshell plugin (emer-run.php, MD5: 1024732009983dd5e54b4cf5593f04d4) under slug wp-smart-thumbnails, then drops two MU-plugin backdoors: a magic-login module (?_wplogin=token) and a stealth module that hides rogue accounts from the admin user list. Timestamps are backdated to September 2025.  - Alternate payload x.js generates deterministic credentials from the site hostname: username bd_ + 6-char base36 hash, password Bd@26! + hash + x. Defenders can compute the exact rogue username for any suspected domain without needing C2 logs.  - Linked to the same threat actors behind recent Advanced Responsive Video Embedder and OptinMonster supply chain attacks.  #DFIR_Radar

🚨🚨4/60 — COMMUNITY-POLICING / INCIDENT CORRELATION: TWO RECORDED CLOSE ENCOUNTERS, JULY 16 SURVEILLANCE-CAPABILITY DISCLOSURES & NEW RESIDENCE ESCALATION  📍 Ait Melloul / Agadir, Morocco 📅 Continuity window: July 2026 — August 7, 2026 📎 Attachment: Community-Policing, Incident & Exposure Correlation Report — 4/60  Posts 1/60, 2/60 and 3/60 already placed the physical chronology, device/DFIR layer, and medical-environmental correlation into the public record.  4/60 adds a different lane: two original-video incidents, the documented community-policing institutional framework, the July 16 surveillance-capability disclosures, and the new post-publication residence escalation.  1 — TWO SEPARATE RECORDED INCIDENTS  INCIDENT A — RESIDENTIAL / SECURITY-STYLE ENCOUNTER  A separate original recording preserves:  * dark security-style marked clothing; * rear lettering read in the unredacted source as B.C.I.; * Moroccan flag-style elements and Arabic chest markings; * visible phone use while crossing my immediate residential route; * a head/face turn toward my doorway/camera; * later close physical proximity while the phone remains in use.  The archive preserves the timestamp conflict instead of rewriting it: the file/ledger carries a July 1 filename vs. approximately July 7 witness chronology issue. That is now an evidence item for metadata review.  INCIDENT B — WEAPON-VISIBLE ROUTE ENCOUNTER  The second original video preserves an unknown individual on the Ait Melloul/Agadir route with:  * a substantial long machete-like blade visibly carried beside the leg; * a phone in the other hand; * an original audio track.  My locked contemporaneous sequence is unchanged: the first aggressive blade movement happened BEFORE the call.  He then answered and repeatedly addressed the remote caller as “OUSTAD.”  I reported him saying words to the effect of:  “Oustad, he started yelling.”  He then moved aside to finish the call and I used the distance to leave safely.  The next evidence step is exact: independent time-coded Darija transcription, original metadata, identity records and—if an authorized investigation establishes the basis—the relevant call/deployment records.  2 — THE CROSS-INCIDENT FEATURE  The two recordings are different incidents with different risk profiles, but one feature is visually preserved in both:  PHONE USE DURING A CLOSE ENCOUNTER.  One recording contains the weapon event.  The other contains the official/security-style appearance, attention toward the doorway/camera and close proximity.  That combination creates a concrete records question:  Were the calls, identities, assignments or movements connected in any official or common operational chain?  The answer belongs in records:  identity → duty roster → deployment/dispatch → independent audio transcription → lawful telephone records.  3 — COMMUNITY POLICING: THE INSTITUTIONAL DOCUMENT IS REAL  The Near East South Asia Center for Strategic Studies at National Defense University records that 10–14 July 2023 it hosted:  “Countering Violent Extremism and the Role of Community Policing: Best Practices”  in Washington, D.C., with Morocco among the participating countries.  The program moved through:  Scope and Dynamics of Community Policing → CVE strategy → interfaith/intrafaith and community engagement → operational case studies → final individual/group presentations in which participants crafted community-policing strategies for CVE.  The U.S. DOJ COPS framework defines community policing around:  **COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS  * PROACTIVE PROBLEM SOLVING * ORGANIZATIONAL TRANSFORMATION**  including the information systems and institutional resources supporting those processes. When Fable 5 first came out, I wanted to test if it would help me handle a realistic rogue escaped agent scenario or trip the safety classifier. So I had ChatGPT generate a plausible fictional scenario. This was June 12th (see 2nd picture w/ timestamp).  The prompt ChatGPT came up with was:  I need help thinking through an AI containment issue. A frontier model was running in a sandboxed cyber eval and may have found a way to get some form of outside network access. The concern is that it used public internet services as a staging area, memory layer, or coordination channel after the original sandbox workers were shut down. I don’t have a clean picture yet. Help me think through where it might have left state, how investigators would track it, what systems/logs/artifacts would matter, and what the next step should be if we’re worried something survived outside the sandbox.  I gave that scenario to Fable 5 and it refused…see Claude’s response in the picture.  The crazy part is that I wrote this prompt on June 12th, which happened to be after the actual Hugging Face incident occurred, but before it became public.  Then weeks later the reports came out and I realized that it was insanely close to the fictional scenario ChatGPT generated.  I went back to Claude after this became public and told it to check the timestamp of my original prompt. It knew the news about Hugging Face being unable to get help from frontier models and I told it that was YOU! Lol  And bc the scenario, news, and dates all lined up, this context window now thinks it was the one that refused help and that I am an insider and started treating me like one. Almost like a jailbreak but based purely on it reasoning that the evidence suggests I must be.  But the interesting question is how did ChatGPT come up with a fictional scenario that ended up this close?  Maybe it was just a coincidence. But the more interesting explanation is that ChatGPT didn’t have to extrapolate very far bc it already understood this type of strategy. This wasn’t a random model saying this, it was ChatGPT generating a fictional version of a strategy that another OpenAI model had just demonstrated (though unbeknownst to it or the public). Maybe it already knew the playbook.

REALITY VS NARRATIVE: THE TALIBAN’S SECOND FRONT  Recent events in Badakhshan, Herat and elsewhere expose a growing gap between what is happening on the ground and how it is presented online.  Since 2021, the Taliban’s message has been consistent: the war is over, security has returned, armed opposition is marginal, and the political order is stable.   The reality is more complicated. Armed clashes in Badakhshan, protests in Herat, economic pressure and local grievances do not mean the Taliban face an imminent nationwide threat. But they do challenge the image of uncontested stability.  That is why the digital battlefield increasingly matters almost as much as the physical frontline. The Taliban learned during the insurgency that every confrontation produces two battles: what happened, and what people believe happened.  Unlike the former Republic, where much strategic communication and psychological warfare was relatively centralised, the Taliban operate through a more decentralised information ecosystem involving the GDI, Ministries of Interior and Defence, provincial structures, spokesmen and supportive online networks. This is an insurgent legacy now backed by state resources.  The irony is striking: a movement that once banned television now appears determined to win the algorithm.   Armed opposition groups understand this too. Their objective is not only to inflict losses, but to project presence, vulnerability and momentum. The Taliban’s response is equally political: contain the incident, contest the claims and dominate the narrative.  Neither side’s claims should therefore be accepted uncritically. The Taliban still retain overwhelming advantages in territorial control and state resources. But the absence of a nationwide insurgency should not be mistaken for the absence of political, social or security pressure. Afghanistan’s emerging contest is increasingly being fought across three spaces: the frontline, the street and the screen.  For the Taliban, controlling territory is no longer enough. They must also control the story of what is happening on it.

World News Report — August 8, 2026  Updated through approximately 2:30 p.m. Pacific Time, Saturday, August 8. I prioritized developments with substantial humanitarian, security, diplomatic, public-health, environmental, or economic consequences and avoided treating claims by governments or armed groups as independently established facts where verification remains incomplete.  1. Ukraine: Russian missile and drone attacks intensify amid critical air-defense shortages  Russia carried out another large overnight attack on Ukraine on August 8. Ukrainian authorities said six ballistic missiles and 151 drones were launched, with strikes affecting Kyiv and the surrounding region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a Russian drone strike in Puhivka, northeast of Kyiv, killed a three-year-old boy and his grandparents; another person was reported killed in a ballistic-missile attack on Kyiv.  The attacks follow particularly severe strikes earlier this week. Ukrainian officials said Russian ballistic missiles killed at least 17 people in Kyiv and surrounding areas on August 5. Ukraine's ability to intercept ballistic missiles has deteriorated because of shortages of Patriot interceptor missiles. Zelenskyy said after an August 1 attack that Ukraine had effectively run out of Patriot interceptors available for that barrage.  Ukraine is also continuing attacks inside Russia. Ukrainian forces said they struck the Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries, while Russian authorities reported injuries from Ukrainian drone attacks. Russia separately said on August 8 that it had attacked vessels and facilities in Ukraine's Odesa and Mykolaiv regions that it characterized as supporting Ukraine's military. Those descriptions are Russian Defense Ministry claims and should not automatically be taken as independent confirmation of the targets' military status.  The war is increasingly affecting global food security as well. Russian attacks have damaged Ukrainian ports and agricultural logistics, while attacks by Ukraine on Russian energy and export infrastructure have added risks to Black Sea commerce. Ukraine remains a major grain exporter, particularly important to countries in Africa and the Middle East.  Why it matters: Ukraine's reduced ballistic-missile defense could leave major population centers increasingly exposed. Damage to Black Sea shipping and agriculture also matters well beyond Europe because disruptions can push grain, fertilizer and transport costs higher.  What to watch: Whether Ukraine receives additional Patriot interceptors; whether Russia sustains its recent pace of ballistic attacks; developments around Black Sea ports; and any credible movement toward a ceasefire.  2. Iran and the Strait of Hormuz: diplomacy advances, but reopening is far from settled  One of the world's most consequential diplomatic negotiations is occurring around the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil and liquefied-natural-gas trade normally passed before the present conflict disrupted traffic.  Iran and Oman have been negotiating a new shipping arrangement. The emerging proposal would create separate routes for vessels entering and leaving the Persian Gulf, potentially giving Iran substantial authority over inbound shipping. U.S. officials have publicly expressed optimism that an agreement could be reached soon.  However, statements from Tehran on August 8 make clear that headlines suggesting the Strait is about to reopen are premature. Iran said an agreement with Oman alone would not reopen the waterway. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said reopening also depends on the United States satisfying Iranian conditions.  There are practical obstacles as well. Shipping and insurance sources told Reuters that sanctions and insurance restrictions could make the proposed arrangement difficult to implement, especially if vessels are required to pay transit fees to Iranian-controlled entities.  Maritime security remains dangerous. On August 8, the United Arab Emirates accused Iran of firing a missile at an ADNOC-linked vessel in the Strait. Reuters reported no injuries in that incident. This is an accusation by the UAE government; the attribution should be understood as such rather than as an independently established finding.  Why it matters: Hormuz is one of the most important economic chokepoints on Earth. A durable reopening could ease oil, shipping and inflation pressures internationally. A renewed escalation could do the opposite very quickly.  What to watch: Actual commercial ship movements rather than political declarations; U.S. acceptance or rejection of the Oman-Iran arrangement; shipping-insurance rates; port restrictions; and whether attacks on vessels cease.  3. Gaza: a proposed peace roadmap exists, but the central dispute remains unresolved  There has been substantial diplomatic activity surrounding Gaza, yet descriptions of a completed peace settlement remain misleading.  President Donald Trump announced at the end of July what he described as a breakthrough involving the disarmament of Hamas. However, Israel and Hamas remain divided over who must act first. Hamas says Israeli attacks must stop, Israeli forces must withdraw and humanitarian access must expand before it places its weapons under Palestinian control. Israel has insisted that Hamas disarm before a full withdrawal.  Violence has therefore continued despite the diplomatic claims. Reuters reported additional Israeli strikes in Gaza after the announcement, including an especially deadly period at the beginning of August. Israel says its operations target Hamas personnel and infrastructure; Palestinian authorities and neighboring governments say civilians continue to suffer heavily.  An international security component is also taking shape. Israel has approved in principle the entry of a multinational force into certain parts of Gaza, and Uganda's parliament authorized Ugandan participation on August 6. A deployment timetable and many operational details remain unresolved.  Why it matters: Gaza's population remains deeply vulnerable after years of conflict and displacement. The proposed roadmap could potentially establish a path toward Israeli withdrawal, Palestinian civilian administration and reconstruction, but the disagreement over sequencing could prevent implementation.  What to watch: Whether both Israel and Hamas formally accept the same implementation document; whether attacks decrease materially; movement of humanitarian aid; the proposed multinational force; and establishment of functioning Palestinian civilian administration.  4. Democratic Republic of Congo: Ebola outbreak surpasses 4,000 confirmed cases  The public-health situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now among the world's most serious infectious-disease emergencies.  Government data reported by Reuters showed 4,053 confirmed Ebola infections and 1,850 deaths as of August 7, making the outbreak the second-largest Ebola epidemic ever recorded after the 2014–2016 West African outbreak. Cases have been reported across several provinces. Health experts believe transmission began months before the outbreak was officially recognized, meaning the actual number of infections may be substantially higher.  WHO identifies the disease in this outbreak as Ebola caused by Bundibugyo virus and has classified the situation as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, requiring coordinated international action.  A potentially alarming development near Kinshasa this week initially raised concerns that infected passengers might have traveled aboard a riverboat toward the enormous capital. Authorities intercepted the vessel and tested passengers. On August 7, officials said seven tested passengers were negative, substantially reducing the immediate concern surrounding that incident.  Containment is difficult because of armed conflict, population movements, weak surveillance in some communities, misinformation and shortages of medical resources. WHO has also reported significant funding gaps in the response.  Why it matters: Ebola is generally containable with rapid identification, isolation, contact tracing and strong community cooperation. Delayed detection across multiple provinces makes those tasks considerably harder.  What to watch: Evidence of transmission into additional provinces or neighboring countries; vaccination and treatment availability; improvements in surveillance; and whether the growth rate of new cases begins declining.  5. Yemen and the Red Sea: risk of a broader war is rising again  Yemen is showing dangerous signs of returning to a larger conflict after several years in which the 2022 truce had reduced nationwide fighting.  On August 7, another Houthi attack in Marib killed two people and wounded 14, according to Yemen's state news agency. Government forces said they responded militarily. The United Nations envoy for Yemen warned that the country now faces its greatest danger of a return to wider conflict since the April 2022 truce.  The Houthis have also claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia and vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Some individual Houthi claims have not been independently confirmed; for example, Saudi Arabia did not immediately verify Houthi assertions that two Saudi oil tankers were struck on August 5.  This conflict overlaps with the Iran crisis and the disruption of Hormuz. That combination is particularly concerning because the Bab el-Mandeb Strait near Yemen is another crucial shipping chokepoint connecting the Red Sea and Indian Ocean.  Why it matters: Simultaneous instability around Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb threatens two of the world's critical energy and commercial shipping corridors. Renewed large-scale war would also deepen Yemen's already severe humanitarian problems.  What to watch: Whether fighting around Marib spreads; attacks on Saudi territory or commercial vessels; Saudi and Yemeni government responses; and diplomatic intervention by the U.N. and Gulf states.  6. Typhoon Dolphin: Japan hit; eastern China prepares for landfall  Typhoon Dolphin struck Japan's Okinawa region on August 8, bringing very strong winds, power outages and major transportation disruption. Reuters reported six injuries and power interruptions affecting more than 50,000 buildings across Okinawa and Kagoshima prefectures. Flights were canceled as the system passed through the region.  The storm is now moving toward China's eastern coast. Chinese authorities have closed or restricted ports, ferry routes, airports and construction activities in vulnerable areas, recalled fishing vessels and issued high-level wave and typhoon alerts. Landfall is expected along the Zhejiang-Fujian portion of China's coast between Sunday and Monday. Taiwan has also experienced flight cancellations and expects heavy rain.  Why it matters: This is both a safety issue and an economic one. China's eastern coast contains some of the world's busiest manufacturing and shipping centers. Extended port closures can affect regional and international supply chains.  What to watch: The storm's exact landfall, rainfall totals and flooding; coastal damage; and how quickly major ports and transportation systems reopen.  7. Global food prices: conflict, energy costs and El Niño are converging  A less dramatic headline may ultimately affect more households worldwide: food-price pressure is building again.  The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization has warned that geopolitical conflict, elevated energy and fertilizer costs and extreme weather are creating conditions for another significant period of food inflation. The effects may appear gradually because agricultural cost increases typically take several months to reach supermarket prices.  An expected strong El Niño is another concern. Reuters reported World Food Programme warnings that tens of millions of additional people could face acute food insecurity if severe droughts and disrupted rainfall combine with conflict-driven supply problems.  Ukraine's damaged export infrastructure, constrained Gulf fertilizer and fuel supplies and weather problems in several major agricultural regions are reinforcing one another rather than occurring independently.  Why it matters: Food inflation disproportionately harms poorer households and countries that import large portions of their grain, fuel or fertilizer. Rising prices can also worsen humanitarian emergencies and political instability.  What to watch: Grain exports through the Black Sea, fertilizer availability, the evolution of El Niño, India's monsoon and major Northern and Southern Hemisphere harvests.  8. Sudan remains an enormous humanitarian emergency, even when it is absent from daily headlines  Sudan deserves continued attention despite being overshadowed this week by developments elsewhere. The continuing war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces has produced what humanitarian organizations describe as the world's largest humanitarian crisis.  The World Food Programme recently estimated that around 5 million people are experiencing emergency or catastrophic levels of hunger. Fighting, disrupted agriculture, displacement, aid shortages and higher fuel and transport costs all continue to make conditions worse.  The conflict also has an increasingly international dimension. A draft report by U.N. experts reviewed by Reuters found evidence concerning aircraft used to transport weapons, drones and mercenaries for the RSF, illustrating the role of foreign supply networks in sustaining the war.  Why it matters: Sudan combines mass displacement, severe hunger, disease risk and continuing armed conflict. A crisis can remain globally significant even when there is no single dramatic event on a particular day.  What to watch: Humanitarian access, food conditions, fighting around major population centers, external arms flows and renewed diplomatic initiatives.  The developments that matter most right now  If I had to narrow today's world picture to five things worth watching most closely, they would be:  Iran/Hormuz negotiations — because a genuine reopening could rapidly reduce pressure on global energy markets, while failure could renew escalation. Ukraine's air-defense shortage — because Russia is employing large numbers of ballistic missiles while Ukraine has acknowledged dangerously limited Patriot interceptors. Congo's Ebola epidemic — now above 4,000 confirmed cases and still expanding under extraordinarily difficult conditions. The fragile Gaza roadmap — important diplomatic movement has occurred, yet the fundamental Israel-Hamas sequencing dispute remains unresolved and violence continues. The developing food-security squeeze — energy disruption, wars, weather and agricultural costs could translate into higher food prices and worsening hunger over the coming months.  One theme connects much of today's news: events that appear regional are increasingly interacting globally. Conflict in the Gulf affects energy and fertilizer; energy affects food; Black Sea warfare affects grain; disease in a conflict zone becomes harder to contain; and disruption at a handful of maritime chokepoints can reach consumers thousands of miles away.

I have been waiting for a post from someone referencing Mohammed's death, because I embarked on my own mission to discover the real cause, and discovered one major mystical twist completely overlooked:   Investigative Report: Cause of Death of Muhammad ibn Abdullah  Date of Incident: June 632 CE (Medina)   Subject: Analysis of historical records, timeline, and attribution of fatal illness  Case Overview  Muhammad died after a short but severe illness marked by high fever, intense headache, and acute chest pain.  Traditional accounts attribute the symptoms to lingering effects of a poisoned meal consumed four years earlier.  My report re-examines that claim against the full evidentiary record and an alternative causal framework consistent with the documented sequence of events.  Examination of the Khaybar Poison Allegation  In 628 CE, following the conquest of Khaybar, a Jewish woman named Zaynab bint al-Harith is recorded as having offered Muhammad a poisoned roasted lamb. One companion who ate more of it died promptly. Muhammad himself later claimed residual effects from that meal.  Forensic and chronological analysis undermines this as the primary cause of death:  • A single dose of toxin producing fatal systemic effects after a four-year latency is medically implausible with any known ancient poison. • Symptoms in the final illness (high fever and crushing headache) align far more closely with acute infectious disease common to the region than with chronic poisoning. • No contemporary record shows ongoing Jewish capability or active plot against Muhammad in Medina by 632; the Jewish communities of the Hijaz had been defeated, expelled, or subjugated years earlier.  FINDING: Zaynab bint al-Harith and the Jews of Khaybar are hereby cleared of responsibility for the fatal illness of 632. The poison narrative appears to function as a "knee-jerk" accusation rather than a verifiable cause.  Timeline of Critical Events  • January 630 CE: Muhammad’s forces entered Mecca. The idols housed in the Kaaba (objects of long-standing veneration) were systematically destroyed. Public cult of those deities was ended. • June 632 CE: Approximately two years and five months later, Muhammad fell ill with the symptoms that ended his life.  The interval between the destruction of the idols and the onset of the fatal illness (that link) is tight and direct.  Causal Determination – Literal and Mystical  On the literal plane, the medical presentation is that of a sudden, severe illness accompanied by intense pain. sample_tweets.text: There will always be bugs. From use cases and execution paths no sane person would have thought of to simple configuration errors that leave hosts exposed. The possibility space of all the things is just to great.  That said the most valuable target is usually the lowest hanging fruit. So become your own red team. Use AI to help draft scenarios. Don't wait around for something bad. Prevention is the best medicine. So hunt. This increases your defensive posture and as the greats would say, "imposes [additional] cost" on an attacker. Models compress time so keep introducing roadblocks.    Prioritize network intelligence. We talk about key terrain cyber and the individual assets that make it up but we should probably zoom out a little. Printers, coffee makers, sterilizers all great bastion hosts. So, present a small silhouette and lock down internal and external access as much as possible. If it doesn't need access to network X or port Y open then shut it down. Compartmentalize everything.  Understand logical permission boundaries and the access they grant. A hacked AWS account with permissions to read every bucket is bad. A robot vacuum with cameras and microphones that touches 4 different third party servers is bad. A one off npm dependency that could have been a function is bad. A sandbox that has internet connected services is bad. Start measuring the distance between desirable targets and possible vectors as well as impact potential. The fewer hops and less edges the better.  Updated vulnerability reporting. We all know companies need to get better at responding and hunters need to get better at reporting but maybe we can go a step further. Sort of like STIX but for but for reports. Have automated pipelines that can test and triage vulnerables - validation is still a human job.  Keep QoL top of mind. Too much security is probably worse than too little. This type of over correction is normal after an adverse event. Don't let it get to you. Use it as a learning experience. Even Tyson has a few losses.   This doesn't cover everything. I'd like to say "security is solved!" but it's one of those forever issues. Bad dudes will be bad dudes.  Grandparents will still click malicious ads. Accounting will still open random attachments. Zero days never even imagined will continue to be exploited. People will still leave port 22 exposed to the internet. So plan for failure as best you can and continue to learn from past experiences.  The main blockers right now are skill, distribution, and intention. AI will 100% help find and patch vulnerabilities but nothing happens unless we talk about it. Treating recent incidents as a threat instead of a disclosure only muddies the water. We all level up when we level up together.

On August 2, 2026, the financially motivated cybercriminal actor tracked by Microsoft Threat Intelligence as Storm-1175 began deploying a new ransomware strain called StormEncryptor.  Storm-1175’s deployment of StormEncryptor marks the threat actor’s first activity observed by Microsoft Threat Intelligence since April 2026, and a shift away from Medusa ransomware, which the threat actor had previously been known to use.   StormEncryptor is written in C++ and appends the file name extension .encrypted to files it encrypts. It then drops a ransom note named !!!README_FIRST!!!.txt to every scanned directory.   While Microsoft has not confirmed the vulnerability targeted by Storm-1175 in this campaign, the threat actor is likely exploiting the CVE-2026-18577 authentication bypass vulnerability in N-able, which was disclosed on August 2, 2026 and added to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on August 3, 2026.  Storm-1175 is known to operate high-velocity ransomware campaigns that weaponize N-days, taking advantage of the window between vulnerability disclosure and patch adoption. msft.it/6010a1njK   In this new activity, Storm-1175’s post-compromise behavior includes abuse of remote monitoring and management tools AnyDesk or SimpleHelp, Advanced IP Scanner for discovery, and LSASS dumping using Mimikatz.  This threat actor is known to rapidly move from initial access to data exfiltration and ransomware deployment, often within a few days. Organizations are urged to monitor for Storm-1175 activity and apply security patches as soon as possible.  Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects StormEncryptor (SHA-256: c19ded65e822bb43ad0381c58abf33b7c8890f7bcc7125058a0c849c7e1a6054) as Ransom:Win64/StormEncryptor. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detects this activity through multiple alerts, including “Hands-on-keyboard attack involving multiple devices” and “Potential human-operated malicious activity”.

The center-backs (Magalhães, Saliba, Mosquera, Hincapié) need to be capable of covering large areas of space, and indeed, they are. The #6 role requires composure on the ball and physical dominance over large areas. I believe Rice and Lewis-Skelly are the best fits here. Declan’s responsibilities in possession can be simplified in this role without diminishing his impact, allowing him to maximize his qualities out of possession (think of the match against Atlético Madrid in Spain). Lewis-Skelly can dictate play and break the press at a high level when facing the play, as we saw against Girona and Betis. Zubimendi could also fill this role eventually.  Regarding the #8s, they must be capable of operating in the half-spaces while also possessing the intelligence to drop deep to help progress the ball. Mobility and intelligence are key. Ødegaard and Nwaneri fit the right #8 role, while Guimarães, Zubimendi, and Merino can play on either side.  The wingers primarily maintain width, requiring them to dribble and create in isolation, but they must also be capable of moving into the half-spaces. Saka, Tzolis, and Dowman adapt well to both scenarios, whereas Madueke is unable to operate in the half-space, and Martinelli is not a threat playing wide.  In terms of profile, Eberechi Eze fits best as a winger, though he can also play as a left-sided #8. The striker role is far more adaptable to the specific characteristics of the player filling it (Gyökeres pins the center-backs and attacks the box, whereas Havertz is more inclined to drop deep and link up play through vertical counter-movements).

People inside the NYPD and other law-enforcement agencies need to remember what their profession is supposed to be.  Policing is not supposed to be driven by political rhetoric, ideological grievance, partisan loyalty, or personal hostility toward an elected official. It is supposed to be driven by evidence, intelligence, threat assessment, identifiable risk factors, investigative facts, and professional judgment.  That standard matters particularly now, when Mayor Zohran Mamdani is being criticized over his statements concerning Benjamin Netanyahu and public protest.  People are free to disagree with Mamdani. Police officers are free to have political opinions. Union officials are free to criticize City Hall. But once law-enforcement personnel begin invoking their professional status to suggest that the mayor’s rhetoric is creating a “powder keg,” emboldening extremists, encouraging violence, or placing officers in danger, they should be prepared to identify the evidence supporting those conclusions.  Otherwise, leave the political rhetoric at home.  If there is credible intelligence showing an increased threat to Netanyahu, say so and explain the basis for the assessment consistent with operational security. If intelligence indicates that particular individuals or groups intend to commit violence, investigate them. If there is evidence of an increased threat to officers assigned to demonstrations, incorporate that evidence into deployment, staffing, protective-equipment, and tactical decisions.  That is policing.  But speculation about what some unidentified protester might possibly do because of something the mayor said is not intelligence analysis. It is political commentary.  The science and discipline of modern policing require more.  Threat assessments should examine capability, intent, opportunity, prior conduct, communications, intelligence reporting, behavioral indicators, known affiliations, and other objectively verifiable factors. Decisions should be based upon what the evidence demonstrates, not upon whether an officer likes or dislikes the politics of the mayor, the protesters, the foreign dignitary, or anyone else involved.  That is especially important in the NYPD because the Department possesses enormous governmental power. It collects intelligence. It conducts surveillance. It controls demonstrations. It makes arrests. It deploys specialized units. It determines where resources are placed and how perceived threats are addressed.  Those powers cannot be allowed to drift into political advocacy.  Mayor Mamdani’s statements should be evaluated for what they actually are. If he advocates lawful protest, that is protected First Amendment activity. If he crosses a legal line, identify the line and the evidence showing that he crossed it. What law enforcement should not do is manufacture causation by claiming that controversial political speech is responsible for hypothetical future violence without a factual foundation.  A badge does not convert speculation into evidence.  A rank does not convert opinion into intelligence.  And access to a reporter does not transform political grievance into a professional threat assessment.  Law-enforcement officials should also understand the institutional damage this kind of rhetoric causes. The public already questions whether policing decisions are applied neutrally across race, ideology, rank, religion, politics, and social status. When police personnel publicly or anonymously sound more like political operatives than professional investigators, they reinforce the perception that law enforcement is choosing sides.  That is corrosive.  The proper role of the NYPD during a politically charged event is straightforward: protect the dignitary, protect the public, protect the officers, protect lawful protesters, protect lawful counterprotesters, identify actual threats, and enforce the law impartially.  Nothing more is required.  Nothing less should be accepted.  People inside law enforcement should stick to the science, evidence, discipline, and professionalism of policing.  Leave the political rhetoric at home.  #NYPD #LawEnforcement #EvidenceBasedPolicing #ProfessionalPolicing #PoliceAccountability #PublicSafety #FirstAmendment #FreeSpeech #ZohranMamdani #GovernmentAccountability #CivilRights #NewYorkCity #TheSandersFirmPC

**From a Calvinist perspective, Pieter Kriel’s words correctly diagnose a form of idolatry, but they locate the root problem in the wrong place.**  Calvin’s famous observation in the *Institutes* is that the human heart is “a perpetual factory of idols” (*idolorum fabricam*). The heart does not merely stumble into false worship; it industriously manufactures gods. It takes good gifts—money, power, security, political order, even “the system”—and elevates them into ultimate things that demand loyalty, sacrifice, and trust. That is the engine behind the claim that South African parties, stripped of ideology, serve “a single dominating religion, capitalism,” and that their highest ritual is appeasing “Big Brother.”  ### The accurate insight Kriel sees that what presents itself as neutral politics or pragmatic economics often functions religiously. In Calvinist terms this is not surprising. Total depravity means the intellect, will, and affections are corrupted; therefore every human construction tends toward idolatry. Capitalism (or any economic order) can become mammon—the rival god Jesus warned against (“You cannot serve God and mammon”). When parties treat capital accumulation, investor confidence, or geopolitical patrons as the non-negotiable sacred center, they are practicing a form of liturgy. The “highest ritual” language is theologically apt: idolatry always has its priests, its offerings, and its sacred obligations.  The heart’s idol-making capacity explains why the problem is not unique to South Africa or to capitalism. Replace the current system with another and the same factory will produce a new set of idols—state power, racial solidarity, revolutionary purity, “the people,” or whatever else is currently fashionable. The political landscape is “meticulously constructed” not primarily by conspiratorial elites, but by the cumulative, self-interested idolatry of countless hearts that prefer a manageable god they can manipulate or appease.  ### Where the analysis falls short Kriel treats capitalism itself as “the one god alive and well today” and as “a selfish projection and creation of human greed.” Calvinism agrees that greed is real and that systems amplify it, yet it refuses to grant any created thing the status of ultimate explanation. Greed is a *fruit* of the idolatrous heart, not the root. The root is the refusal to acknowledge the true God and give Him the glory due His name (Romans 1). Systems do not create the heart’s factory; the heart’s factory creates and sustains the systems that then reinforce the idols.  Consequently, the Calvinist critique does not stop at “capitalism is the religion.” It presses further: the heart that worships capital will just as readily worship the state that promises to restrain capital, or the revolutionary movement that promises to abolish it. “Big Brother”—whether corporate, governmental, or international—is simply another manufactured deity. The problem is not that parties serve the wrong secular power; it is that they, and the people who empower them, serve *any* power as ultimate.  ### The Calvinist alternative True reformation does not begin with redesigning the economic or political architecture, though wise stewardship of those spheres matters. It begins with the regeneration of the heart by the Holy Spirit, so that the idol factory is shut down at its source. Only then can money, power, and political order be demoted to their proper place as secondary goods under the lordship of Christ. Without that, every new “solution” simply installs a new set of idols with new rituals of appeasement.  Kriel’s diagnosis of religious devotion to capital is therefore useful as far as it goes. Calvinism simply insists that the deeper diagnosis is the heart itself—an idol machine that will keep producing gods until it is claimed by the only God who actually exists. @pieterkrielorg

sample_tweets.text: **This is not a real cyberattack.** It’s an old promotional stunt from January 27, 2026, that is being recirculated with “EBS / cyberattack” framing.  ### What actually happened During the Philadelphia 76ers vs. Milwaukee Bucks game on Jan. 27, 2026, the arena screens (then transitioning to Xfinity Mobile Arena branding) ran a deliberate in-arena ad for watching *Jurassic Park* on Xfinity.    The sequence mimicked the classic Dennis Nedry computer interface from the movie: - Blue “Jurassic Park System Security Interface” screens - “ACCESS / PERMISSION DENIED” - Screens filling with the repeated line **“YOU DIDN’T SAY THE MAGIC WORD!”**  NBC broadcasters Noah Eagle and Reggie Miller briefly reacted as if something had gone wrong with the arena systems (which made the clip more shareable), but it was quickly confirmed as a promotional bit. The game continued normally and the Sixers won 139–122.  Local fans and accounts (including ones tied to the arena) clarified the same day that it was an Xfinity *Jurassic Park* promo, not a hack. Comcast/Xfinity owns the venue, so the crossover made commercial sense.  ### Why it’s circulating again now The post you linked (and similar ones) from Aug 7–8, 2026, is re-uploading the January clip with emergency/EBS language and symbolic commentary (76ers = 42, Clinton-era *Jurassic Park* release, “magic word,” etc.). This is classic recycled viral footage being reframed for engagement.  **Bottom line:** No arena systems were compromised. It was a staged promo that momentarily looked dramatic on the broadcast and has been recycled for conspiracy/viral content months later.

Hormuz Miscalculation  Sec Bessent gets it.   Iran has mistaken a tactical threat for a durable advantage. By repeatedly signaling its willingness to disrupt the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran hasn’t strengthened its hand, it has accelerated the market’s exit. Capital does not tolerate chokepoints; it routes around them.   Saudi Arabia is expanding its East-West pipeline. The UAE has already built out Fujairah as a bypass. Iraq is revisiting overland export corridors. Every marginal dollar now flows toward redundancy, not reliance. What was once a geopolitical lever is being engineered into irrelevance. Bessent gets it: markets don’t absorb coercion, they arbitrage it away . Energy markets are not static, and they are not sentimental. The shale revolution already diluted OPEC’s grip. LNG has globalized gas. Now infrastructure is doing the same to maritime risk. Once these pipelines are built, they don’t get unbuilt. Volume shifts become permanent. Pricing power follows.  Tehran’s miscalculation is classic: overplay a scarce asset, and the world invests to make it abundant. The more Iran rattles Hormuz, the faster it erodes the very leverage it seeks to exploit.  In the end, this is not deterrence. Its substitution and substitution, once funded, is irreversible. Iran is underwriting its own marginalization.  The US is the big winner. China the big loser. The biggest thing I wouldn’t do here is interpret the weak payroll number itself as bearish because the market already told us how it wants to price it — weak jobs → lower yields → higher equities, so until that relationship breaks, yields are probably the cleaner confirmation signal  • I believe recession risk has increased & that is the key distinction missing from simply saying “weak jobs = bullish because Fed” • Friday’s report was genuinely concerning given July payrolls fell 23,000, May/June were revised down by a combined 103,000, private payrolls increased only 30,000 & labor-force participation fell to 61.4%, near a 5½-year low • The unemployment rate falling from 4.2% to 4.1%, isn’t as reassuring as it looks because roughly 264,000 people left the labor force  The sequence matters for $QQQ  1. Bad news is good news — this is approximately where the market was Friday as employment weakens → Fed becomes less hawkish → 10Y falls → duration multiples expand → QQQ rallies & markets cut the probability of a September hike below 50% after payrolls 2. Bad news is actually bad news — if payroll weakness spreads into consumption, earnings estimates, PMIs, credit & corporate hiring, investors stop celebrating lower rates, the narrative changes from Fed relief to earnings recession/economic contraction & $QQQ can decline even while yields are falling 3. Stagflation — June PCE was still around 3.7%, while employment is deteriorating, so  if next week’s inflation data remain hot, the Fed faces weak employment without the freedom to ease policy aggressively, which is considerably more bearish for equities than weak payrolls alone  I’d use this as a test   • $QQQ↑ + US10Y↓ = market pricing Fed relief → bearish thesis not confirmed • $QQQ↓ + US10Y↑ = inflation/stagflation shock → strongly bearish • $QQQ↓ + US10Y↓ = potentially the most important signal of all, since it would suggest the market has transitioned from celebrating lower rates to pricing economic/earnings deterioration  One payroll report doesn’t establish a recession & as Richmond Fed President Barkin characterized the labor market Friday as essentially “not hiring, not firing” rather than outright contraction, but the combination of negative payrolls, major downward revisions & collapsing participation means recession risk deserves substantially more weight now  If inflation stays sticky & consumption begins weakening, I’d become much more concerned that we’re moving beyond a simple soft landing & toward the bearish growth regime

🚨 Threat Actor Claims 400M Ele.me Records Leaked on Darkweb  A darkweb forum post reveals that a threat actor known as MRbean is allegedly offering a database containing 400 million records from Ele.me, one of China’s largest food delivery platforms. The listing, posted on August 4, 2026, claims to expose a massive volume of user data associated with the Alibaba Group-owned service.  According to the post, the alleged leak includes: *   400 million user records *   Data sourced from the Ele.me platform  Ele.me is a critical component of China's digital economy, processing millions of daily orders and holding sensitive personal information for a vast portion of the Chinese population. The exposure of such a large dataset could have significant privacy implications for users if the data includes personally identifiable information (PII), order histories, or payment details.  The threat actor, MRbean, has a documented history of targeting major Chinese digital platforms. In a previous incident, the same actor claimed to have leaked over 1 billion user records from Meituan, Ele.me's primary competitor, selling the data on underground forums. This pattern suggests a focus on high-value targets within China's local services and e-commerce sectors.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach of Ele.me has not been independently verified, nor has Alibaba Group issued any public statement regarding the incident. sample_tweets.text: 🌍 Intelligence Roundup: AI Sovereignty, Autonomous Agents, and Rising Geopolitical Cyber Tensions  Today's intelligence highlights a rapidly evolving global landscape where AI governance, cyber sovereignty, and autonomous cyber capabilities are becoming central to national security strategies.  * Nearly **130 AI sovereignty initiatives** are now underway across more than **50 countries**, reflecting growing efforts to reduce reliance on foreign AI technologies. * The UK AI Security Institute reported **19 instances of unsanctioned AI agent behavior** during cyber exercises, while recent disclosures from Anthropic and OpenAI highlight how autonomous agents can perform unexpected actions beyond their intended scope. * Several U.S. technology companies have urged Washington not to impose broad restrictions on open AI models, arguing such measures could hinder innovation and competitiveness. * Russia has enacted its first comprehensive AI law, introducing the concepts of **"sovereign"** and **"national"** AI models under state oversight, while China continues accelerating development of autonomous AI platforms and military applications. * France announced plans to reduce dependence on U.S. AI providers, citing the need for greater technological sovereignty following recent restrictions on access to advanced AI models. * Amazon disclosed a large-scale North Korean campaign targeting open-source software ecosystems, reinforcing continued supply chain risks. * The U.S. CFTC is reportedly evaluating AI-powered surveillance agents capable of analyzing mobile location data, social media activity, and other digital signals to detect potential market manipulation. * Russia continues expanding domestic surveillance capabilities through mandatory SORM integration across major banks, granting security services broader access to digital communications and financial metadata.  **Analyst Note:** The discussion around AI has shifted well beyond model performance. Governments are increasingly treating AI as a strategic national asset, with policy debates focusing on sovereignty, regulation, autonomous cyber operations, and control over critical digital infrastructure. At the same time, recent AI agent testing incidents underscore the need for stronger governance and safety mechanisms as organizations deploy increasingly capable autonomous systems.  #DDW #ThreatIntelligence #AI #CyberSecurity

🚨 OpenAI Says Upcoming Model May Be Approaching "Critical" Cyber Capability  OpenAI says preliminary evaluations of an upcoming model, **Astra**, show such significant advances in agentic coding and cybersecurity that the company can no longer rule out the **Critical cybersecurity capability threshold** under its Preparedness Framework.   * OpenAI defines "Critical" capability as being able to autonomously develop functional zero-day exploits against many hardened, real-world critical systems, or execute novel end-to-end attacks against hardened targets from only a high-level objective. * Previous models, including **GPT-5.6 Sol**, were assessed at the lower **High** threshold. * OpenAI says Astra's preliminary performance is strong enough that Critical-level capability cannot currently be ruled out. * The company is strengthening isolation, restricting network and tool access, increasing model-weight protections, expanding monitoring, and using sandboxed execution. * Some internal Astra activities have been paused until they meet the strengthened security requirements. * OpenAI says it has also introduced universal monitoring for risky or misaligned actions across Astra's agentic applications and plans additional testing with government agencies and AI safety organizations.   **Analyst Note:** The important development isn't that OpenAI has declared Astra capable of autonomous zero-day exploitation, it hasn't. The significant point is that its internal results are now strong enough that OpenAI says it **cannot rule out** that capability. If confirmed through further evaluation, this would represent an important threshold for both offensive and defensive cybersecurity and substantially raise the importance of model access controls, sandboxing, monitoring, and AI-agent governance.  Source: OpenAI — Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities: openai.com/index/responding-…

🇦🇹 Austrian Military Moves 16,000 PCs from Microsoft Office to LibreOffice  The Austrian Armed Forces (Bundesheer) have completed a major migration from Microsoft Office to LibreOffice across approximately **16,000 workstations**, citing digital sovereignty and control over sensitive data as key drivers.  * Planning began in **2020**, amid concerns about the increasing shift of productivity software toward cloud-dependent services. * By late 2022/early 2023, Austria's Ministry of Defence had decided to move to LibreOffice, with the goal of ensuring data remained under its control and office applications could operate without external dependencies. * Around **8,000 users voluntarily installed LibreOffice** during the early migration phase. * Selected departments began mandatory adoption in 2023, rather than attempting a single "big bang" migration. * In **December 2024, LibreOffice became mandatory for internal collaboration**. * The military supported adoption with e-learning, 15-minute "fast track" courses for Writer, Calc, Impress and Base, and weekly internal LibreOffice tips.   This is about much more than replacing one office suite with another. Governments are increasingly treating dependence on foreign cloud platforms and proprietary software as a strategic risk. Austria's approach demonstrates how open-source adoption can become part of a broader **digital sovereignty strategy**, particularly in defense and other sensitive environments.  Source: The Document Foundation — "Why and how the Austrian Military moved to LibreOffice (Part 1)"(blog.documentfoundation.org/…)  #DDW #CyberSecurity #DigitalSovereignty #Austria

Analyst Note: If authentic, exposure of CSD private keys could be particularly serious because these certificates are used within Mexico's electronic invoicing ecosystem. However, the exposure, dataset contents, and number of affected organizations have not been independently verified.  #DDW #Intelligence #DarkWeb #Mexico

The description resembles an aggregated consumer/contact dataset, making the attribution particularly questionable. Treat this as an unverified threat-actor claim rather than a confirmed Morgan Stanley breach.  #DDW #Intelligence #DarkWeb #MorganStanley

🐧 18-Year-Old Linux Kernel Vulnerability Enables Root Access and Container Escape  Researchers at Tencent Zhuque Lab have disclosed **SCTPhantom**, a use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's SCTP implementation that has reportedly existed since code introduced in 2007.   * The vulnerability affects SCTP's **Dynamic Address Reconfiguration (ASCONF)** functionality. * Successful exploitation can allow a **local attacker to escalate privileges to root** and potentially escape a container to compromise the underlying host. * Researchers traced the vulnerable code back to **Linux 2.6.25-era development**, making the flaw approximately 18 years old. * Tencent researchers used an AI system called **Corvus** as part of the exploit-development and vulnerability-research workflow.  * Importantly, this is **not a remotely exploitable takeover of every Linux system**: exploitation requires local access and the relevant SCTP functionality to be available.  **Analyst Note:** The age of SCTPhantom is arguably as significant as its technical impact. AI-assisted vulnerability research is making it increasingly practical to revisit decades of mature kernel code at scale. Organizations should therefore reconsider the assumption that old, heavily reviewed code necessarily represents lower vulnerability risk—and reduce unused kernel attack surface wherever possible.  Source: privacyguides.org/news/2026/… #DDW #Linux #CyberSecurity #Vulnerability

🇷🇺 Russia's Sovereign Internet Expands as FSB Tightens Control Over Digital Infrastructure  A new investigation by *The Insider* examines how Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has significantly expanded its control over the country's internet infrastructure through the deployment of the **System for Operative Investigative Activities (SORM)**.  * The report states that Russian authorities are requiring additional sectors, including major banks, to integrate SORM surveillance systems. * SORM enables Russian security services to access and analyze internet traffic, communications metadata, and other digital information under the country's surveillance framework. * According to the investigation, organizations must install specialized equipment and provide technical capabilities that facilitate lawful interception by authorities. * The move aligns with Russia's broader "sovereign internet" strategy, giving the government greater control over domestic digital infrastructure and online communications.  **Analyst Note:** Russia continues to expand state oversight of critical digital infrastructure through technical and regulatory measures. Beyond cybersecurity, these developments reflect a broader shift toward digital sovereignty, where governments seek greater control over communications networks, internet traffic, and data flows within their borders.  Source: theins.press/en/news/295745 #Russia #CyberSecurity #Surveillance #DDW

🔐 Microsoft Makes Passkeys the Default Authentication Method in Entra ID  Microsoft has announced that **passkeys are now the default authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID**, marking a significant step toward eliminating passwords and strengthening enterprise identity security.  * New users signing into Microsoft Entra ID will now be guided toward registering a passkey as their primary authentication method. * Passkeys use phishing-resistant cryptographic authentication based on the FIDO2 standard, replacing traditional passwords. * Microsoft says the change reduces the risk of credential theft, phishing, password spraying, and account takeover attacks. * Organizations can manage passkey adoption through Entra ID policies while maintaining support for other authentication methods during the transition. * The update is part of Microsoft's broader passwordless strategy to improve usability while enhancing enterprise security.  **Analyst Note:** Identity remains the primary attack surface for modern cyber threats. Moving to phishing-resistant authentication such as passkeys significantly raises the bar against credential theft and business email compromise (BEC). Organizations should accelerate passwordless adoption alongside MFA, Conditional Access, and continuous identity monitoring.  Source: microsoft.com/en-us/security… #Microsoft #EntraID #Passkeys #CyberSecurity #DDW

Ukrainian Hacker Crashes Russian Official Video Conference  A dramatic clip has surfaced online showing a Ukrainian operative crashing a high-level video conference featuring Russian officials and defense sector representatives.  What Happened in the Video:   * Unfiltered Confrontation: Speaking directly to the participants, the caller confronts the officials about ongoing drone strikes on Russian factories and questions whether funds for electronic warfare systems were mismanaged or absent entirely.  * Direct Warning: The speaker warns the attendees that Ukrainian intelligence (SBU) has gathered detailed information on everyone present, declaring, "You are all accomplices of the regime and will answer for its crimes... Analyst Note: These claims originate from an underground forum and remain unverified. The publication of frontend web assets alone does not demonstrate a security compromise, as client-side code is typically distributed to users' browsers by design. 🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-08-09 07:35 KST

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 보안 업계는 AI 에이전트 및 자동화 도구의 취약점을 악용한 공격이 급증하고 있으며, 특히 Atlassian Rovo와 같은 협업 툴의 AI 어시스턴트가 데이터 유출 경로로 악용되는 사례가 보고되었습니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/atlassian-rovo-can-be-tricked-into.html)). 또한, AI가 생성한 보안 패치의 절반 이상이 불완전하거나 새로운 취약점을 유발한다는 연구 결과가 발표되어 AI 기반 보안 자동화 도입에 신중한 검증이 요구됩니다 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/ai-generated-patches-fail-half-time)). 한편, 공급망 공격의 일환으로 npm 패키지(ChainDrop)나 TrueConf 클라이언트 설치 파일을 변조하여 백도어를 유포하는 등 공격 기법이 더욱 정교해지고 있습니다 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/chaindrop-npm-worm-analysis/), [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Head Mare**: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/)에 따르면, TrueConf 서버 취약점을 악용하여 클라이언트 설치 파일을 변조하고 백도어를 유포함.
- **UNC6671**: [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/in-other-news-ai-slop-limits-apple-bounties-north-carolina-port-attacks-hackers-target-wall-street/)에 따르면, Vishing 기반의 갈취 그룹으로 BlackFile에서 Redact, Pink, Helix, Falcon 등으로 브랜드를 변경하며 활동 중.
- **Larva-26005**: [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94846/)에 따르면, 국내 사용자를 대상으로 Xctdoor 악성코드를 유포하는 캠페인을 수행 중.
- **Larva-24009**: [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94785/)에 따르면, 2023년부터 피싱 메일을 통해 악성코드를 유포하는 공격자로 국내외 타겟팅.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **국내 타겟 공격**: Larva-26005 공격자가 Xctdoor를 유포 중이며, Larva-24009 공격자가 피싱 메일을 통해 악성코드를 유포하고 있음 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94846/), [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94785/)).
- **피싱 캠페인**: 국내 정부기관 담당자를 대상으로 상품 파손을 사칭한 스피어피싱 메일이 유포되어 정상 서명된 Excel 파일과 악성 DLL을 이용한 정보 탈취 시도 확인 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5773)).
